intro: Eleven hundred metres down, the cable went slack and the radio went strange. What came back up the line was not speech. The divers say the deep hums through the hull at night, low enough to feel in the fillings of your teeth, and that the only way to sleep through it is to let the sound find its own shape in your skull. In the mess, every cup and tin hangs from its own hook above the table, and each hook has been shaved and bent by hand until the thing it holds sits level and still, no two alike. Their hands remember the fit of the copper rod, the wrench, the dented pot, better than their own names.
echo: Tennyson wrote that it sleeps below the thunders of the upper deep, and will rise only once.
